name: login-line-escape

graded_by.test: core/internal/recording/ (the file is the recording lane's to name) — a login value holding controls, a C1 character, DEL and a backslash is written escaped, in exactly these bytes: owed by the Release A recording plan

description: The escape rule of the login line, shown on one frame: a code-6 frame whose text holds an ESC sequence, a CR LF, a C1 character (U+0085), DEL, a backslash and non-ASCII text. The line stays one printable row: ESC is written \x1b, CR and LF \x0d and \x0a, U+0085 \x85, DEL \x7f, the backslash two backslashes, and the non-ASCII characters stay as UTF-8. A classic player that replays the recording prints the row and acts on no control in it. A supplied login asks nothing, so a recording of one holds no code-6 frame; the frame is here because the line format is fixed once for both codes, and the text of a prompt may come from the device, which is not trusted.
